messages.author: 66aaf5d139ba9c7f
messages.subject: Re: best practices for modular Shiny app development?
parts:
The main thing for me (sofar) was to try to keep ui.R manageable. 

In ui.R I have a line:

uiOutput("ui_analysis")

That calls a function defined in server.R (see below). I put all analysis tools I want to use into a directory (tools/ in this case). These are sourced when the app is started up. I then have a tools.html file that, basically, determines which ui elements get shown. Ideally I would want tools.html to be created automatically based on what is in the tools/ directory. Haven't gotten that far yet but suggestions on how to do this cleanly are welcome.

Code is here:

https://github.com/mostly-harmless/radyant

I hope Alex will pitch in as well. His approach is likely to be a bit more sophisticated than mine.

Keep us posted as you make progress with your app.

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

# source base functions
source('radyant.R', local = TRUE)

# source enabled analysis tools
flist <- sourceDirectory('tools', recursive = TRUE)

# the 'grand' analysis ui-element caller
output$ui_analysis <- renderUI({
  if(input$tool == "dataview") return()
 get(paste('ui_',input$tool, sep=""))()
})
})

messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Re: best practices for modular Shiny app development?
parts:
I should start by stating that I haven't built any Shiny apps of the magnitude that Vincent or Alex have built. However, I thought that it would be useful to share my approach, since it is a bit different from their approaches.

My app is usually structured in the following fashion

|- apps
|- www
|------libraries
|----- index.Rmd
|----- index.html
|- server.R

All apps are single files in the app folder, which are sourced into server.R, which is generic

require(shiny)
shinyServer(function(input, output){
  addResourcePath('libraries', 'www/libraries')
  apps = dir("apps", pattern = '^app', full = T)
  for (app in apps){
    source(app, local = TRUE)
  }
})

I prefer to use the HTML UI, especially when I have a lot of text. I use Slidify to convert index.Rmd to index.html in the www folder.

You will find an example of this approach in this github repo https://github.com/ramnathv/shinySlidify, which you can run using

runUrl("https://github.com/ramnathv/shinySlidify/archive/gh-pages.zip")

Note that the page layout can be changed easily as Slidify supports multiple frameworks. So you can do a bootstrap page instead of slide deck.

Best,
Ramnath
